title: BN1 - An Adventure Game / City Crawl set in the modern city of Brighton
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VTOl1gAKo44

Daniel (@dungeondive) takes a detour from dungeons to BN1, a city crawl set in modern-day Brighton from Paul Stapleton and Bedsit Games, the people behind his beloved Popper's Ladder. You play a tourist attempting the most interesting possible day; first to fifty anecdote points and back to Brighton Station wins.

It looks like an old-school roll-and-move and then quietly isn't. Each of the five characters — showgoer, explorer, sightseer, shopper, historian — carries a bespoke twelve-card action deck, drawn four at a time and spent completely before reshuffling, where identical movement values carry different bonuses. Bus day-savers, cabs, busking with a bought instrument, provisions eaten in parks for random benefits, shop decks full of memorabilia, and oversized destination cards offering choices with real press-your-luck teeth.

What Daniel keeps returning to is the local lore. The encounter deck is stuffed with real Brighton eccentrics — Max Miller, Doreen Valiente, Fatboy Slim, and George Montague and Disco Pete, to whom the game is dedicated. There's also a rule forbidding you from counting spaces on your own turn, which he reads as simulating the hustle of an unfamiliar city.

It left him thinking about designing a game around his own Californian hometown, and wishing Stapleton had better distribution outside the UK.

----

Which real place would you most want turned into a board game — and would the local detail land for someone who's never been?
